request_byte_scope: Actual change mutation request bodies: begin JSON + full tar or gzip manifest + missing part PUT bodies + commit body. Excludes headers, HTTP responses and transport overhead. upload_payload_bytes retains only PUT content/part bodies.

commit_timing_scope: Proxy request entry to upstream commit response headers, including forwarding its request body; excludes downstream response consumption.
download_timing_scope: Fixed-version public GET through the proxy to a local tar file; validation hashing and tar inventory are timed separately.
restore_timing_scope: Real AgentMoor CLI restore version 1 wall time, including download, validation and atomic publish; excludes the subsequent inventory comparison.

kubernetes_validation.note: These are host CLI/HTTP measurements. Integrated Kubernetes validation is a separate pending run; no cluster success is claimed here.

limitations: All samples are single sequential synthetic runs on one host, not repeated controlled trials or a production performance SLO.

Counts include actual change mutation request bodies: begin metadata, gzip manifest or full tar, missing body PUTs and commit. They exclude HTTP headers, response bodies and transport overhead; they are not total network traffic.

The measurement proxy creates a new upstream HTTPConnection per request and closes both directions; the threaded proxy and connection setup amplify many-small-request costs. Times are not direct production latency.

The client already uploads up to 8 bodies concurrently. Catalog UploadPart serializes object Put and each per-body operations.updated write under its lock. Local object file/directory Sync and SQLite FULL autocommit costs exist, but their individual runtime shares were not profiled.

Preparation and commit perform per-object existence checks; commit fully rereads and hashes the logical tar. S3 additionally incurs per-object HEAD/GET requests. Savings in upload bytes do not imply faster sync or restore.
Unchanged workspaces return before the transfer mode is selected and send no change mutations; the observed no-op time differences do not establish a parts-algorithm regression.
Large samples use distinct 4096-byte synthetic bodies. A single-file change may affect multiple chunks for larger files, and manifest cost depends on file count, paths and tar framing.
No native runtime CLI, model, Kubernetes Job, restart, cancellation, publication fault injection or Worker Pod loss is executed by these benchmark runs.

PostgreSQL/S3 backend identity is independently attested by server versions, image IDs/digests, revision rows, S3 object presence, and absence of SQLite/local objects; this is fixture attestation, while sync/download/restore use public HTTP.
Local SQLite library version was not recorded. Existing baseline evidence keeps its original source identity and is not replaced by this aggregate.
